solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ignore past appearance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fail to notice or pass over
second meaning, split in two: a word for past followed by a word for appearance

explanation.surface: Advice to disregard how someone used to look.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a charade read as one phrase: OVER means past (as in 'the match is over') and LOOK means appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to miss it or let it pass, a standard synonym of ignore.

clue.text: Pacific island with nothing, then a hospital and university

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An island in the Pacific with nothing at first, then later a hospital and a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island where Honolulu stands, in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Avoid restaurants perhaps with unlimited seating?

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: the word taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Is endless seating a reason to stay away from restaurants?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, flagged by 'perhaps' and '?': to eat in is to have a meal at home, one way of avoiding restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating in means having your meal at home rather than going out, so it is one way to skip dining out.

clue.text: Small folk for whom plain suit ill tailored

indicators.note: something tailored is cut and remade, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: the letters of all three words are taken as fodder

explanation.surface: Tiny people, for whom an ordinary suit has been badly cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The inhabitants of Lilliput in Swift's Gulliver's Travels are six inches tall, so an off-the-peg suit would indeed fit them badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliputians are the tiny people of Gulliver's Travels, and the word now means very small persons generally.

clue.text: As champagne no longer being kept perhaps in the workplace

definitions.text: As champagne no longer being kept perhaps
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a bottle taken out of its bucket of frozen water
second meaning: a room or building where people work at desks

explanation.surface: Champagne left out to go warm at an office party.
explanation.walkthrough: Champagne is kept on ice; once it is no longer kept that way it is OFF ICE, which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a room or building where administrative work is done, a common kind of workplace.

clue.text: Brought up some loaves maybe, as announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: loaves are an example of the baked staple, which sounds identical

explanation.surface: Someone carried a few loaves upstairs, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' looks like carrying the loaves upstairs, but it means raised, as a child is.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred is the past tense of breed, meaning reared or raised, the same as brought up.

clue.text: Rice dish, so dry, covered in port!

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by something else, so these letters sit inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous port
taken as written
TT means teetotal, and a dry person drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A rice dish so dry it had to be drowned in port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine; here it is the harbour city Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock, so it is a rice dish.

clue.text: Initially not anybody could compose this Irish song

indicators.note: to compose is to put together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: At first, nobody at all could have written this Irish ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny Boy is the much-loved ballad sung to the Londonderry Air, regarded as an Irish song.

clue.text: Early morning exhortation to Polish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cheerful call to get out of bed
second meaning, playfully: polishing makes something come up and gleam

explanation.surface: A wake-up call delivered in Polish?
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P disguises 'polish', to make shiny; the setter treats getting something to come up and gleam as a whimsical sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the customary jolly command to get up out of bed at dawn and be lively.

clue.text: Place to stay following golf

definitions.meaning: first meaning: somewhere guests book a room
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the code word for H comes straight after Golf for G

explanation.surface: Finding accommodation after a round on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet runs Foxtrot, Golf, Hotel, India, so the word that follows Golf is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering rooms to travellers, so it is literally a place to stay.

clue.text: By day, small boy gives shudder

parts.note: FRI is the short form of Friday, a day
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: During the day a little lad makes someone shiver.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden thrill or shiver of excitement or fear, which is a shudder.

clue.text: So tactless in recording film in bank

indicators.note: one thing set in another means the film's letters go inside the word for bank

parts.note: the first in is taken as written
a disc is a recording, as in a record or CD
to bank on someone is to rely on them
E.T. is Spielberg's famous film

explanation.surface: Someone tactlessly records a film on a disc while in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first supplies letters as written, the second is the container signal. To bank on someone is to rely on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting indiscreetly means acting without discretion, in a manner lacking tact, so 'so tactless' describes the adverb.

clue.text: Word of objection in attempts to make compliments

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the objection goes within the attempts

parts.note: tries are attempts
'but' is the word that raises an objection

explanation.surface: Raising an objection while attempting to pay compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tributes are expressions of praise or respect, which is what compliments are.

clue.text: About to beat famous racehorse

parts.note: re is Latin for about, as in 'regarding'
to drum is to beat rhythmically

explanation.surface: Someone is about to beat a well-known horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's most famous steeplechase, three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum is the celebrated British steeplechaser, three-time winner of the Grand National at Aintree.

clue.text: Kid, torn, resolved to make toast

indicators.note: something resolved is worked out anew, so the letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words are taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A conflicted child decides to make some toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like grilled bread, but it is the verb meaning to raise a glass to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to raise glasses and drink in their honour, which is to drink to them.

clue.text: Entirely skint otologist? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only a part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Is a penniless ear doctor fully broke, or only partly?
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money; an otologist is an ear specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for as a whole, meaning completely or entirely.

clue.text: Good innkeepers producing spirits

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
innkeepers are hosts to their guests

explanation.surface: Kindly publicans bringing out the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' in a pub suggests strong drink; here it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are the apparitions of the dead, often called spirits.

clue.text: Ibis slithers all over the place in these lands

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of both words are taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A wading bird slides around all over these countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Isles are the group of islands, Great Britain and Ireland among them, off northwest Europe: a collection of lands.

clue.text: Some rotten nuisance: the result of "all work and no play"?

definitions.text: the result of "all work and no play"

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a piece of the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Endless toil is a rotten nuisance that leaves us jaded.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'all work and no play makes Jack a dull boy'; the answer is that dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and weariness, the dullness the proverb says comes from endless work.

clue.text: Raise flag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lift, as a car is lifted with a lever device
second meaning: a small flag flown at a ship's bow, as in the Union flag's common name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as hoisting a flag, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up a car is to lift it, and a jack is a ship's flag indicating nationality, as in Union Jack.

clue.text: Proceeds to place labels around family

indicators.note: 'to place ... around' says one thing is put round another, enclosing it
around tells us the labels wrap round the word for family

parts.note: tags are labels
kin is family

explanation.surface: Someone goes on to stick name tags on their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' reads as a verb, 'goes on', but it is the noun meaning money taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money received by a business, which is what its proceeds are.

clue.text: Old Greek colony with aliens on it, periodically returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the kept letters are read backwards
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek settlement keeps being revisited by aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the ancient region of Greek settlement on the west coast of Asia Minor, a colony of Greek cities.

clue.text: Winter weather in south at present

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
now means at present

explanation.surface: It is currently wintry down in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen precipitation typical of the cold season, so it is a kind of winter weather.

clue.text: Star, losing heart, takes terrible chance

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the next word is dropped
terrible suggests something badly messed up, so the letters left are jumbled

parts.note: the five-letter word without its middle letter
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A celebrity, losing courage, gambles badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star, losing heart' looks like one unit, but the comma ends the definition: it is 'takes' that loses its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in printing, so a star in typographical terms.
